Similar triangles hidden in chords.

Goal: I can use intersecting chord, secant, and tangent segment relationships.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Chords crossing inside: (one chord's pieces multiplied) a times b = c times d. Two secants from P: PA times PB = PC times PD (outside piece times whole secant). Tangent and secant from P: PT2 = PA times PB.

Each comes from similar triangles. For crossing chords AB and CD meeting at E, draw AC and BD. Angles CAB and CDB intercept the same arc, and the vertical angles at E are equal, so triangles AEC and DEB are similar by AA, giving AE/DE = CE/BE.
